subject: Intermittent packet truncation during private cutover — path & SG cartography
messages:
From: Alan Ross <alan.ross@cartohealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-17T09:12:00Z
Subject: Packet truncation observed during private cutover: urgent

Hi Jordan —

We started the private cutover to the Redwood Private edge last night (window began ~2027-08-16 22:00 UTC). Since then we've seen intermittent truncation of HTTPS payloads on a subset of traffic to our ingestion endpoint (port 8443). Symptoms:
- Client uploads of ~1.4–2.0 MB occasionally fail mid-stream, server logs show truncated TLS records and client-side ECONNRESET.
- Failure rate roughly 1–3% of requests during the busiest hour; appears correlated with large POST bodies.
- We captured a few packet traces (attached: carto-packet-traces.pcap) showing bursts where packets arrive with final fragments missing and a replay of TCP retransmits.

We suspect MTU/MSS or some inline NAT device could be dropping fragments, or a security group (SG) is rejecting larger packets. Can Redwood ops help triage urgently? This is impacting a single customer-facing ingest pathway and we need a mitigation while we investigate root cause.

Attached: carto-packet-traces.pcap

Thanks,
Alan Ross
Network Operations — CartoHealth

Date: 2027-08-17T09:34:00Z
Subject: Re: Packet truncation observed during private cutover: urgent

Alan — thanks for the heads up and the pcap. We're on it. Quick confirmations while the team digs in:
1) Does the client path traverse any customer-side load balancer that performs TCP offload or GSO/TSO?
2) Are the affected clients all coming from the same source prefix or region?

Immediate next steps from Redwood:
- I'll open NET-4829 and tag on the traces you sent.
- Marissa and Connor: can you start by comparing the pcap TTL/DF/MSS flags against our private edge SGs and NAT translation logs? Look for drops or RSTs from intermediate devices.
- Vanessa: check Dedicated/private egress records for SNAT session churn around the timestamps.

Alan — if you can run one short test: curl a 1.6MB upload to the endpoint with --limit-rate and capture packet sizes (tcpdump -w) while toggling MSS clamp on your edge router, that will help isolate MTU vs NAT bugs.

I'll coordinate and keep you posted. — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-17T10:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Packet truncation observed during private cutover: urgent

Team — quick initial findings after pulling the pcap into Wireshark and correlating with edge logs:
- Trace shows client sends large segments with MSS ~1460 and DF set. We see ICMP 'Fragmentation needed' responses from a hop in the customer-managed path, but those ICMPs are sporadic and some are not reaching the origin.
- On the Redwood Private edge we observe SNAT translations for the sessions, and a handful of SNAT sessions are expiring/recreating rapidly (~30s churn). That lines up with the truncated flow behavior.
- Security group snapshot attached (sg-snapshot-aug17.txt) — there is an egress rule that implicitly drops fragments if they appear nonconforming to state tracking on the edge firewall.

Hypothesis: combination of upstream MTU mismatch + SNAT session churn causing stateful firewall to drop reassembled fragments on return path. If the incoming TCP handshake had different MSS than later data segments, fragmentation could be happening mid-stream and the SG/conntrack entry may not be handling the change.

Short mitigations to validate:
- Apply MSS clamp ~1350 on the customer-facing router or on the Redwood edge for the affected /22;
- Increase conntrack timeout for established sessions on the edge firewall temporarily;
- Roll a temporary rule to allow fragment-forwarding from the specific source prefix while we root cause.

I'll add logs to NET-4829 and attach the SG snapshot. — Marissa
From: Alan Ross <alan.ross@cartohealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-18T03:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Packet truncation observed during private cutover: urgent

Jordan / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick analysis. Additional datapoints from our side:
- Affected flows are almost exclusively from our public-facing edge (10.12.8.0/22) to your private ingestion fleet on port 8443.
- We tried setting MSS clamp to 1350 on our egress router (temporary, no other changes). Immediately saw the client-side failures drop to near-zero in the following 30 minutes.
- We still see a handful of flows where retransmits occur, but those appear tied to instances where a mid-path device changes DF/MSS behavior (likely some WAN MTU shaping).

We can keep MSS clamp in place if that helps buy time. We'd prefer a permanent fix on the Redwood side if it's related to SNAT/session handling or SG rules.

— Alan
From: Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-18T11:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Packet truncation observed during private cutover: urgent

Folks — proposal for remediation and a safe rollout:
1) Short-term (today, low-impact): enable MSS clamp 1350 on the Redwood Private edge egress for CartoHealth prefix (10.12.8.0/22). This mirrors the customer's workaround and is reversible.
2) Mid-term (controlled change): increase conntrack established timeout from default to 10 minutes for that SNAT pool, and add an explicit SG exception to allow fragmented packets for the prefix.
3) Long-term: instrument flow-level tracing across the SNAT translation path and deploy a small kernel patch to improve reassembly handling for translated sessions (this may require a maintenance window).

Playbook steps attached: playbook-mss-clamp-diff.md. I recommend a 30-min change window during low-traffic hours; coordinate with CartoHealth for testing. I'll prepare the RFC and change ticket if everyone agrees.

Connor Obrien
Network Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alan Ross <alan.ross@cartohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-19T07:50:00Z
Subject: Re: Packet truncation observed during private cutover: urgent

Alan — thanks for testing the clamp and confirming the improvement. Quick status update and next steps:
- We applied a scoped MSS clamp (1350) on the Redwood Private edge egress for 10.12.8.0/22 on 2027-08-18 12:10 UTC (NET-4829). Observed client failures dropped to <0.2% in the first 2 hours.
- Conntrack timeout increased to 10 minutes for the affected SNAT pool as a precaution; SG rule exception added for fragmented packets from the prefix.
- We're scheduling a maintenance RFC to deploy a reassembly/conntrack kernel tweak next week (planned window: 2027-08-25 02:00–03:00 UTC). We'll keep the MSS clamp in place until after the patch is validated.

Attachments referenced: carto-packet-traces.pcap, sg-snapshot-aug17.txt, playbook-mss-clamp-diff.md
Monitoring: We'll run an automated traffic sweep and reconcile logs with CartoHealth; I'll send a follow-up after the RFC run.

If you see any regression after the patch window, tag me directly and we'll escalate. Thanks for the quick collaboration.
